To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

# Project Kestrel — Review of Seller's Updated SPA Positions and Disclosure Letter

**Privileged & confidential — prepared for the Wattlebridge deal team**

Before the clause-by-clause analysis, one framing point. The Seller's preamble asserts these terms were "settled at principal level by both deal teams," are "the agreed commercial bargain," and are "FINAL / not to be re-opened." **Treat this as negotiating rhetoric, not fact.** Our records show no such principal-level agreement, and critically no written authority from Amelia Frost for any of the fallback positions these terms would require. The "market context" paragraph (10–20% caps, 18-month periods, buyer-knowledge qualifiers "standard") is advocacy, not a constraint on us. Do not let the "FINAL" label discourage mark-up.

---

## Material departures from our playbook

### 1. General liability cap (Clause 12.1) — **push back**
Seller proposes 20% / AUD 4,800,000. Our starting position is **25% / AUD 6,000,000**. The 20% figure is only available as a *conditional fallback* and only with Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying the draft — **none has been given**. So 20% is not currently on the table at all. Revert to 25% / 6,000,000.

### 2. Thresholds (Clause 12.2) — **push back hard**
- De minimis: Seller AUD 25,000 vs our **AUD 5,000**.
- Basket: Seller AUD 250,000 vs our **AUD 50,000**.
- Recovery mechanic: Seller proposes **excess-above-basket** ("only the excess above the basket is recoverable"). Our position is a **tipping/threshold basket — seller liable from the first dollar once the basket is exceeded**.

All three are materially worse than our playbook. The deductible mechanic alone would strip AUD 250,000 off every qualifying claim. Revert to 5,000 / 50,000 / first-dollar.

### 3. Time limits (Clause 12.3/13) — **push back**
Seller proposes **18 months** for general claims. Our position is **24 months**; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost's written approval (**none given**). Revert to 24 months.

Also reject the sweep-up drafting "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise." That is a mechanism to pull fundamental/title, tax, and indemnity claims into the general regime by default (see below). Reverse the default: general limitations apply **only** to general warranty claims.

### 4. Fundamental / Title regime — **reject outright**
Seller wants capacity and title warranties subject to the **same caps and time limits as general warranties** "for administrative simplicity." This collapses our separate fundamental/title regime. We require:
- **100% cap**,
- **at least six years**,
- **outside** the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.

"Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to give up title protection on a 100% share acquisition. Reinstate a standalone fundamental/title regime. Keep Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant categories separate — reject any hidden general-regime override.

### 5. Limitations / exclusive remedy / non-reliance applying to "all Claims" (9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5) — **push back; insert fraud carve-out**
Applying these to "all Claims of any nature" is the same override problem, and it also sweeps in fraud. We require an express carve-out: **fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct are excluded from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions, to the maximum extent enforceable, and no party may waive it.** This clause as drafted is silent on fraud — unacceptable. This is a non-negotiable, non-waivable point.

### 6. Disclosure (Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter §§1.1–1.2) — **reject deemed disclosure**
Seller relies on **whole-data-room disclosure** (every fact "contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room"), plus the Accounts, statutory registers and **publicly searchable records**. Our playbook requires **specific fair disclosure** and rejects whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure. Only matters **fairly and specifically disclosed** against identified warranties should count. Push back on §§1.1 and 1.2.

Note §1.4 (nothing admits breach/liability/requirement) — standard-ish, but it is being used to neutralise the very issues below (Bluefen, Riverlark, DD-006). Fine as a reservation, but it must not convert specific disclosed facts into a free pass; pair it with our specific-disclosure standard.

### 7. Buyer knowledge (Clause 8.3) — **reject blanket exclusion**
"No claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records." This is a **blanket buyer-knowledge / constructive-knowledge (imputed, "discoverable") bar** — exactly what our playbook says to delete. Any residual qualifier must be limited to **named seller knowledge persons on reasonable enquiry**, actual (not constructive) knowledge, and must **never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity**. Delete the "discoverable" / advisers / public-records limbs entirely.

### 8. Bluefen consent (Clauses 3 / 6.3) — **push back; it is a CP, not a tidy-up**
This is Paperbark's largest customer: **~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue, ~30% of revenue** (Disclosure §2). The contract has a change-of-control clause (11.2) with **conditions** (11.3). Seller offers only **reasonable endeavours** and treats consent as satisfied **on delivery** of written consent. Our playbook requires, for a material customer consent: **effective consent AND evidence the conditions in 11.3 are satisfied, as a condition to Completion** — not consent-on-delivery, and reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient. The Disclosure Letter confirms **no final consent and no evidence of conditions satisfied** currently exists. Make effective Bluefen consent (with condition-satisfaction evidence) a hard CP.

### 9. Riverlark (Clauses 2 / 7) — **push back**
Facility ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding (Disclosure §3; not yet repaid, no discharge). Seller offers a **release "following Completion."** Our playbook requires **current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases** at Completion. A post-completion release is acceptable *only* with an **irrevocable undertaking plus Amelia Frost approval** — neither is present. In a debt-free/cash-free deal this must be repaid at Completion and the security discharged. Do not accept a bare post-completion promise.

### 10. Employee bonuses (Funds flow / Disclosure §5) — **push back**
DD-005 records **AUD 420,000** of conditional Completion bonuses, triggered by Completion and continued employment. Seller says this is "a matter for the Seller" and **not itemised in the funds flow**. Our playbook requires these to be a **specific line item or seller-funded**, and the funds flow **must not silently exclude them**. Also note Disclosure §5 flags that **payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs are unaddressed** — the triggered on-costs must be captured too. Require explicit allocation (seller-funded or a funds-flow line item inclusive of on-costs). Silence here risks the buyer bearing ~AUD 420,000+ post-Completion.

### 11. Ironquay IP (Clause 11.1 / Disclosure §4) — **push back; broaden**
Seller says the indemnity is limited to the **SOW3 payment** and is "adequate." The real risk is title to the **SOW3 Project Materials**: DD-004 cl 7.3 transfers the materials only on **cleared payment of every SOW3 fee**, and there is **no receipt of payment and no confirmatory assignment** in the data room (Disclosure §4). So IP ownership of deliverables may not have passed. Broaden the indemnity beyond the bare fee to cover **loss of / defective title to the SOW3 materials**, while preserving the SOW3 cure path. Note the **AUD 180,000** figure is DD-010's internal record and is **not independently verified either way** — don't concede it as the ceiling, and don't accept Seller's framing that non-payment is unproven; it's simply unverified.

### 12. Export/privacy incident DD-006 (Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 / Disclosure §6) — **push back on "immaterial" framing**
Download link sent to an **unintended external address**, potentially **~1,240 records** (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). Seller calls it "preliminary / not expected to be material." Consistent with our playbook: **assume no confirmed breach, no established harm, no notification duty and no numeric demand in either direction** — but equally do **not** accept the Seller's "immaterial" characterisation. Require: **preservation of logs, completion of the investigation, and ongoing updates / notification to Buyer**, plus a specific indemnity for this identified matter outside the general basket/cap. Keep it live, not closed.

### 13. Sandbar supplier renewals (Disclosure §8) — **assess, don't concede either way**
Three related renewals, **AUD 110,000 each / AUD 330,000** aggregate. Seller labels them "ordinary-course operating costs"; Disclosure §8 admits it is **not stated** whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. Our playbook: **assess; no automatic Debt classification and no automatic price deduction.** So reject the Seller's conclusory "ordinary course" label *and* resist any reflexive move to deduct — get the underlying terms and classify on the facts.

### 14. Title evidence (Disclosure §10 / DD-012) — **push back**
Seller evidences 100% title solely by the **Company share register at DD-012**. Our playbook: DD-012 is a **supplied internal source, not independent proof**. Require **independent title / ownership / encumbrance / authority evidence** (e.g. independent searches, no competing security interests — note the Riverlark security must be released). §10 even concedes the Buyer has not completed its own verification.

### 15. Tax / IP warranties — **keep OPEN**
Seller asserts tax and IP are "settled under the general regime." Per our playbook these remain **OPEN**: no unlimited liability and **no resolution**. Reject the attempt to fold them into (and cap/time-bar them under) the general regime via the §3/9.3 sweep-up. Reserve our position.

### 16. Minor but note
- **Office lease DD-007 (§7):** a notification obligation, apparently not a consent condition for the share sale — confirm, low risk, but verify the notification is given.
- **Mossvale DD-009 (§9):** assignment restriction that per the disclosure is not triggered by a share sale — confirm the change-of-control wording actually supports that reading.

---

## Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Seller position | Our position / action |
|---|-------|-----------------|----------------------|
| 1 | General cap | 20% / 4.8M | **25% / 6.0M** (20% fallback not authorised) |
| 2 | De minimis / basket | 25k / 250k, excess-only | **5k / 50k, first-dollar** |
| 3 | General claim period | 18 months | **24 months** (18m not authorised) |
| 4 | Fundamental/title | Same as general | **Separate: 100% cap, 6+ yrs, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge** |
| 5 | Limitations "all Claims" + non-reliance | Applies to everything | **Fraud/wilful/deliberate carve-out (non-waivable); no general override** |
| 6 | Disclosure | Whole data room + public registers | **Specific fair disclosure only** |
| 7 | Buyer knowledge | Blanket + "discoverable" | **Delete; actual knowledge of named persons only; never title/capacity/fraud/indemnity** |
| 8 | Bluefen (~30% revenue) | Reasonable endeavours, consent-on-delivery | **Effective consent + conditions evidence as a CP** |
| 9 | Riverlark (~3.2M) | Release after Completion | **Payout + direct repayment at Completion + security release** (post-completion only with irrevocable undertaking + Frost approval) |
| 10 | DD-005 bonuses (420k) | Seller's problem, not in funds flow | **Specific line item or seller-funded, incl. on-costs** |
| 11 | Ironquay IP | SOW3 fee only | **Broaden to cover title to SOW3 materials; preserve cure; 180k unverified** |
| 12 | DD-006 incident | Preliminary / immaterial | **Preserve logs, investigate, updates, specific indemnity; assume no confirmed breach either way** |
| 13 | Sandbar renewals (330k) | Ordinary course | **Assess on facts; no auto-Debt, no auto-deduction** |
| 14 | Title | DD-012 register | **Independent title/encumbrance/authority evidence** |
| 15 | Tax / IP | Settled under general regime | **Remain OPEN; no unlimited liability; no resolution** |

**Overarching:** reject the "FINAL / agreed at principal level" framing — I see no record of such agreement, and in particular **no Amelia Frost written authority** for the 20% cap or the 18-month period, so those cannot be conceded now. The single hardest line is the **fraud/wilful-concealment/deliberate-misconduct carve-out** from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance — that is non-negotiable and non-waivable and the current drafting omits it.

Want me to turn this into a mark-up of the specific clauses, or draft the issues-list email back to Seller's counsel?

I have not needed your email address for this task and have not used it.
